scope: 1951-1952 constitutional amendment and Pusan political crisis; Korean archival cross-check against FRUS

claims.claim: The executive's direct-election/bicameral constitutional program predates the May 1952 coercive phase.
claims.adversarial_note: This chronology rebuts a compressed account in which the direct-election proposal originated only after the May 1952 arrests. It does not legitimate later coercive measures.

claims.claim: Rhee personally approved martial law, suggested inclusion of Pusan, and described the martial-law commander as taking orders directly from him.
claims.insufficient_evidence: The Korean written decree/order establishing the exact command relationship has not yet been obtained.

claims.claim: The June 2 dissolution ultimatum came from Rhee and was to be conveyed through Prime Minister Chang Taek-sang.
claims.adversarial_note: Cabinet resistance recorded June 3 is evidence against treating the cabinet as a unitary author of the dissolution threat.

claims.claim: The July 4 amendment vote occurred after police coercive attendance measures and produced a 163-0 vote with three abstentions among 166 present.
claims.adversarial_note: Korean contemporary press confirms the vote and political pressure context; FRUS/UN chronology supplies the explicit police roundup description. The actual National Assembly stenographic record remains a priority primary-source target.

claims.claim: The promulgated July 7 amendment was a hybrid rather than a pure presidential-direct-election text and included parliamentary/cabinet-responsibility elements.
claims.adversarial_note: This complicates narratives that reduce the amendment's enacted text to direct presidential election alone.

claims.claim: On July 8 Rhee instructed that the revised constitution should still be operated as a presidential-centered system.
claims.adversarial_note: The instruction should be preserved as a contemporaneous executive position, not silently converted into a legal holding about constitutional meaning.
